headline: Penang's 520% tourism surge: who counts the arrivals and who pays the rent
context: Malaysia's Middle East arrivals fell 40% in March 2026. Penang pivoted hard to China, India, and ASEAN: 161,599 Chinese tourists in nine months, 61 weekly flights. George Town's heritage core has long depopulated.

changes.summary: Correction: In two cards, replaced unverified heritage-core figures (50,000 to 9,000 residents; 80% lost since 2008) with a statement that the core has long been losing residents.

Correction: the context still said George Town's heritage core "lost 80% of residents since UNESCO listing". The 8 Apr 2026 correction (commit d05813ef8) removed that unverifiable figure from the cards but missed the context.

cards.big: 520% more Chinese tourists landed in Penang, but the success story has a rent bill attached
cards.sub: Penang runs 61 weekly flights to China and projects 8M airport passengers in 2026. The 520% surge uses a low 2023 base of 26,056. George Town's historic core has long depopulated.

cards.big: China generated RM20.87B in tourism receipts nationally. The 'low-value tourist' claim doesn't survive the data.
cards.sub: Post-pandemic Chinese FITs spend 40% more than pre-pandemic group tourists. The real gap is segment, not nationality. MOTAC has no Penang-specific spending breakdown published.

cards.big: George Town's UNESCO core has experienced long-term depopulation: renters of every ethnicity, not one community
cards.sub: B40 renters, women hawkers, Indian Muslim traders and Chinese clan tenants face the same economics: a tourist night earns more than a month's rent.

cards.big: Penang has a sustainable tourism master plan, but nobody is measuring whether it works
cards.sub: No carrying-capacity study for the UNESCO zone. No displacement tracking. Airport expanding to 12M capacity by 2028, but water, waste, and housing haven't scaled alongside.

cards.big: This isn't about Chinese tourists versus heritage. It's about who profits from growth and who pays rent.
Penang needs a public dashboard tracking residents, rents, and local retention, not just arrivals
